January 4th would have been Peter Steele's 55th birthday. He died of an aortic aneurysm in April 2010.

Pete Steele was from my hometown, and even though I was a fucked up teenager who didn't care about much, I was proud of that. Type O Negative was my favorite band. They were one of only 3 live concerts I've ever been to see. The second was a concert my mom took me to when I was like, 3, because she couldn't find a sitter, and the third was a guest appearance by the Boston Pops in NH a few years ago. The did a bunch of Shakespearean stuff (Tchaikovsky, Mendelssohn, and a few others.)

Type O Negative dissolved when Pete died. In the words of drummer Johnny Kelly, "When Peter died, Type O Negative died with him."

It's been so many years since I even listened to them. I only remembered today because we got on the subject of music at work, and I mentioned Type O. I just got finished listening to some of their music, and it felt good. I still love it exactly as much as I did back then.

I'm sorry I've been forgetting you, Pete. I'll try and remember January 4th from now on. I miss you man.

Fun fact: Nathan Explosion was based on Peter Steele and George Fisher of Cannibal Corpse.
